books.title: Annihilation of Caste
books.summary: An undelivered address turned self-published manifesto. Ambedkar dismantles the moral and economic defences of the caste system and calls for the destruction of the religious sanction behind it.
keyIdeas: Caste is a division of labourers, not of labour
Real reform requires breaking the authority of the Shastras
Political democracy cannot survive without social democracy

books.title: The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution
books.summary: Ambedkar's D.Sc. thesis for the London School of Economics, analysing the history of the Indian currency and arguing for a gold-standard rupee with a fixed exchange value.
keyIdeas: A stable currency protects the poor from hidden inflation
The gold-exchange standard was mismanaged by colonial authorities
Monetary policy is a question of social justice

books.title: The Evolution of Provincial Finance in British India
books.summary: His Columbia University doctoral thesis, tracing how financial relations between the central and provincial governments developed under British rule.
keyIdeas: Centralised finance concentrated power and stifled provinces
Fiscal federalism needs clear, rule-based devolution
Budgets reveal the real priorities of a state

books.title: Who Were the Shudras?
books.summary: A historical inquiry arguing that the Shudras were once Kshatriyas of the solar dynasty who were degraded to the fourth varna through conflict with the Brahmins.
keyIdeas: Varna rank was historically contested, not divinely fixed
The fourfold order was imposed, not natural
History can be used to unsettle inherited hierarchy

books.title: The Untouchables: Who Were They and Why They Became Untouchables
books.summary: A companion volume to Who Were the Shudras?, proposing that untouchability arose from the treatment of 'broken men' who remained Buddhist after the Brahminic revival.
keyIdeas: Untouchability has a datable historical origin (~400 CE)
Beef-eating became a marker of stigma after it was abandoned by others
The disability is social engineering, not pollution

books.title: Thoughts on Pakistan / Pakistan or the Partition of India
books.summary: A dispassionate examination of the Muslim League's demand for Pakistan, weighing the case for and against partition on communal, military and administrative grounds.
keyIdeas: Communal majorities and minorities cannot be wished away
If partition happens it must be complete, including transfer of population
A house divided against itself cannot be defended

books.title: States and Minorities
books.summary: A memorandum on fundamental rights submitted to the Constituent Assembly, containing an early blueprint for constitutional safeguards and 'state socialism' in key industries.
keyIdeas: Rights on paper need remedies and institutions
Economic structure should be part of the Constitution
Minority protection is a test of majority good faith

books.title: The Buddha and His Dhamma
books.summary: Published posthumously, this is Ambedkar's reconstruction of the Buddha's life and teaching as a rational, this-worldly ethics of liberty, equality and fraternity.
keyIdeas: Dhamma is morality, not ritual or metaphysics
Suffering has social as well as personal causes
Religion should be judged by whether it upholds human dignity

books.title: Riddles in Hinduism
books.summary: An unfinished critical commentary on contradictions in Hindu scripture and practice, released decades after his death by the Government of Maharashtra.
keyIdeas: Sacred texts contradict one another on basic questions
Reason must be allowed to test revelation
Reform means confronting the texts, not evading them
